clue.text: Lawrence had dinner between setbacks with private conversations

parts.note: T.E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, gives his initials

indicators.note: one piece is placed between the two halves of the other

parts.note: read as 'sets back': the word set turned round, twice over
had dinner means ate

explanation.surface: Lawrence of Arabia dines amid his reverses, then has quiet talks.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence of Arabia was T. E. Lawrence; 'setbacks' is read as two words, sets back, so the reversal happens twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tete-a-tete is a French-derived term for an intimate talk between two people.

clue.text: Optimism on Matthew's part: is his obese female child male, even if model?

indicators.note: only a part of the name is taken, the run inside it

parts.note: taken as written
obese means fat
her is the female pronoun
a tot is a small child
he is the male pronoun
even if means though
the Model T, Henry Ford's car

explanation.surface: A bizarre question about whether a fat woman's child is a boy, framed as a gospel's optimism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' takes THEW from the end of Matthew's; the rest is a long charade with 'is his' taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says we believe what we hope is true, a description of wishful optimism.

clue.text: See 1
Fight that is a danger to sheep

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A brawl that threatens a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal brain disease of sheep, so it is a hazard to them.

clue.text: See 1
Brown field in Surrey at disposal

indicators.note: letters at someone's disposal can be arranged as they please, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brownfield site in Surrey is available to be sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown field' looks like brownfield land; it means Gordon Brown's field of work, as Chancellor of the Exchequer heading the Treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Brown ran the Treasury as Chancellor, so it was his area of responsibility.

clue.text: Church or garage with link to the web

definitions.meaning: a church holds services and a garage services cars, so each supplies a service
a company that supplies internet access

explanation.surface: A church or a garage gets online.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a church and an internet company supply services, the first religious and the second internet access.

clue.text: The creed of the Mendicants?

parts.note: read literally: what people who live by begging believe in

explanation.surface: A question about the doctrine of the begging friars.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means is hard to credit; read literally it is what those who beg believe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something incredible, read literally as the faith held by those who live on alms.

clue.text: King has clue to things from chivalrous figures

parts.note: K for king, then NIGHTS with ERRANT as an anagram signal is a clue to the word things

explanation.surface: A monarch holds the key to the deeds of chivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a clue, 'nights errant' tells you to rearrange NIGHTS into things; add K for King in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Knights errant were medieval knights wandering in search of chivalrous adventure.

clue.text: Nonsense some celebrated with return of person with pick

indicators.note: the pieces are read from the end to the start

parts.note: rot means nonsense

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the word are used, its first four

explanation.surface: Some rubbish was cheered when the man with the pickaxe came back.
explanation.walkthrough: ROT plus CELE (from celebrated) is turned backwards by 'with return of' to give ELEC + TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector has a vote, so is someone who gets a choice; pick here is a choice, not a tool.

clue.text: Occupy with achievement of bowler and batsman

parts.note: in cricket a bowler completes an over of six balls
a batsman's achievement is a run

explanation.surface: Taking the crease, with work done by both the bowler and the batter.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, and a run is the basic unit a batter scores.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun a territory is to swarm over and occupy it.

clue.text: Big band music on second side

parts.note: a wing is a side, as of a building or a team

explanation.surface: Big band music played on the B-side.
explanation.definitionFit: Swing is the jazz style of the big bands of the 1930s and 1940s.

clue.text: Flower of the 15-a-side game on time

parts.note: rugby union, played by teams of fifteen, abbreviated RU
hr is the abbreviation for hour, a period of time

explanation.surface: A rugby match kicking off on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword trick for a river, something that flows; the Ruhr is a German river.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is a thing that flows, a river, and the Ruhr is one in Germany.

clue.text: Speculate on limit to hospital department's raising of standard

parts.note: to bet is to speculate
a term is a limit or end
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

explanation.surface: Gambling on the end of a hospital unit's drive to raise standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Betterment is improvement, the raising of a standard of living or condition.

clue.text: It's hell to do crosswords — get lost

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hell
to solve is what one does with crosswords

explanation.surface: A frustrated solver complains that crosswords are hell and tells them to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve is to melt away or vanish, so to disappear.

clue.text: "Animal Behaviour" is a title by composer

indicators.note: a composer puts things together, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A book titled Animal Behaviour written by a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composer' looks like the author but is the anagram signal for IS A TITLE BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestiality is brutish or beastlike conduct, behaviour fit for an animal.

clue.text: Indian city won back by chance

parts.note: luck means chance

explanation.surface: An Indian city won back by sheer luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucknow is the capital of the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.

clue.text: Report of infliction of pain on arsonist?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: torture is the infliction of pain

explanation.surface: An account of an arsonist being tortured.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who torches buildings, a made-up word for an arsonist, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Actor in boot?

definitions.meaning: a boot ... is a shaped form kept inside a boot

explanation.surface: A performer stuck in a boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Beerbohm Tree was a famous stage actor, and a shoe or boot tree keeps footwear in shape.

clue.text: Large quantities (see advertisements)

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
ads is short for advertisements

explanation.surface: A note directing readers to the many adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads is the informal word for lots, great amounts of something.

clue.text: Motorist's eccentric stream

definitions.note: read as motorist is, a noun followed by is

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
a river is a stream

explanation.surface: A driver's oddball stream of thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is a person who drives a car, so a car driver.

clue.text: Relating to a branch that causes alarm

indicators.note: the answer is the word that, rearranged, produces the word alarm

explanation.surface: A branch whose very name frightens.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is anagrammed to make alarm, so the letters of alarm give it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramal is a botanical adjective meaning of or belonging to a branch.

clue.text: More than 50% of English tortoises are rank

indicators.note: more than half of the word is kept, its opening six of eight letters

parts.note: Chelonia is the zoological order of tortoises and turtles

explanation.surface: A statistic that most English tortoises are smelly.
explanation.walkthrough: CHELONIA is the order of tortoises; 'More than 50% of' keeps its first six letters, a little over half.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a level or grade in an organisation, a rank.

clue.text: Parliamentarian, one in hell with the wrong polarity

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
a magnet's poles are north and south, so south is swapped for north

parts.note: Hades is the classical underworld, hell
one parliamentarian, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament in hell with his magnetism reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' leans on 'Parliamentarian' for its sense, an MP; 'with the wrong polarity' swaps the magnetic poles S and N, turning HADES into HADEN. John Hampden was a 17th-century English politician.
explanation.definitionFit: John Hampden was a leading Parliamentarian who opposed Charles I before the English Civil War.

clue.text: King Edward cut down amid rebel riot by little bird

indicators.note: one piece goes in the middle of the other
running riot, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the name taken as written
R is for rex, king

explanation.surface: King Edward is struck down during a rebellion beside a small bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' scrambles the letters of rebel into REBLE, 'cut down' drops the last letter of Edward, and R, the Latin rex, means king.
explanation.definitionFit: The reed warbler is a small brown songbird of reedbeds.
